summary: Lita Peipina works in Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under Jens Braarvig in 2003, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Lloyd W. Pflueger works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1949–1959), and the University of Munich (~1970–1974), where he earned his Dr.phil.

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. After studying at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso, he founded and served as head of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (~1973–1997).

Lobsang Jamspal (born 1936) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. His career includes posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, University of Delhi, and Columbia University.

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Pema Chok Palzangpo, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Lobsang Shastri specializes in Tibetology. He served as Head Librarian at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tenpa works in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He completed a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

Lobsang Tenzin (born 1939) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held teaching and leadership posts at the Central School for Tibetans in Shimla (1961), Darjeeling (1964), and elsewhere (1965–1970), and served as Director of CIHTS (~1971–2000).

Lobsang Yongdan is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kumbum Monastery and Cambridge (PhD, by 2014) under Hildegard Diemberger, later holding postdoctoral posts at the University of Bonn and Max Planck Institute.

Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959) and under Tenzin Gyatso, served as director of Tibet House New Delhi (1964–1966), and joined the University of Bonn in 1966.
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.
Lodrö Sangpo works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner, founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996, and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra (1927–2022) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. Educated at University of the Punjab and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, he held leadership roles at the International Academy of Indian Culture, ICCR, and ICHR.
Longlian (1909–2006) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. She studied under Fazun in 1939 and under Nenghai Shi from circa 1941 to 1967.

Lore Sander (1936–2023) was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and Central Asian studies who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt. Her appointments included curator at the Museum of Asian Art (1987) and posts at the Free University of Berlin.

Lori Meeks (born 1976) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her BA at Columbia and PhD at Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone, later becoming Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at USC in 2004.

Lorna Dewaraja (1929–2014) worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Ceylon and University of London, and held faculty appointments at the University of Peradeniya (~1965–1978) and University of Colombo (~1978–1989).

Lothar Ledderose (born 1942) is a sinologist and art historian educated at Bonn, Heidelberg, Princeton, Harvard, Tokyo, and Cologne. He served as professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2010) and president of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

Lothar von Falkenhausen (born 1959) is a sinologist and archaeologist. Educated at Bonn, Peking University, and Harvard (PhD ~1982–1988), he taught at UC Riverside (~1991–1993) and became a professor at UCLA in 1993.
